audit.why: Packet win rate 52.71% over 129 games matches MC_WR_TABLES.zac.aurora = 52.71. No elo-tier language in either layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer is built around 'Twofold Hunt', which is not an Aurora ability. It occupies 25 writable strings including focus.text, and four of them write it as 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)'.
audit.why: Two errors stacked. The name is a corruption of Twofold Hex, which is Aurora's Q — a curse missile with a recast that drags the curse back through you. But the ability the guide is describing is plainly not a Q: it calls it 'Her escape', tags it '(Blink)', and full.focus.letters is ['W']. Aurora's W is Across the Veil, a leap that turns her invisible on landing. So the generator took the wrong ability's name, mangled it, and attached it to the right slot. The content layer independently gets the mechanic right ('her W blink slips your engage') while never naming it, so the two layers describe the same ability under a name that does not exist. This is the same failure mode as the fabricated 'Repeating Dashes' in zac__ambessa, and again suspectNames is empty, so the automated near-miss check caught neither.
audit.corrected: Replaced every occurrence with Across the Veil, and collapsed the redundant 'Across the Veil (Blink)' forms. focus.letters is already ['W'] and needs no change, which confirms the slot was right and only the name was wrong.
sources: champ-data/_kits/aurora.json Q 'Twofold Hex' and W 'Across the Veil'

audit.whatIsWrong: focus.text is 'Aurora Twofold Hunt' — the fabricated name is what the loading screen shows.
audit.why: Same defect as focus.text in the Ambessa entry. It is the single most visible string in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Should read 'Aurora Across the Veil'. NOT proposed as an edit: the current string is 19 characters and the correct one is 22, which is +15.8% and outside the applier's band. It needs a manual write or a band exemption for focus.text.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.whys[4] and content.spikes[1].text call Between Worlds a 'double-blink R'. It is not a blink pair.
audit.why: Riot's text: Aurora 'leaps in a direction, releasing a shockwave that damages and slows any enemies it hits. Afterward, she creates an area that slows enemies within it and allows Aurora to teleport from one side of the area to the other.' It is one leap plus a persistent slowing zone she can cross repeatedly. That distinction is the whole counterplay — the zone is a fixed piece of ground with two sides, so you can position relative to it, which you cannot do against a free double blink. The guide's version tells the player the situation is hopeless when it is actually readable.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both to describe the zone and its crossing, and gave the 140s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Weirding is never mentioned in either layer.
audit.why: Riot's text: it 'damages and slows enemies before Aurora hops backward to safety'. That makes it a second disengage on a 15/14/13/12/11s cooldown, far shorter than Across the Veil's 22s. The entire matchup is framed as 'bait her one escape, then commit' — with a second, more frequent escape in the kit that framing gets Zac killed, because he spends a 21s Elastic Slingshot believing she is out of outs.
audit.corrected: Added The Weirding and its 15s cooldown and 825 range to breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: _missing-interactions.json flags that Zac's Elastic Slingshot denies Aurora's Across the Veil and Between Worlds, and nothing in either layer states it. content.wants.you[0] says only 'Bait her W blink before committing your slingshot' — the opposite instruction.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot's knockup is the reason the engage works: an airborne target cannot cast, so a landed E denies the blink outright rather than merely preceding it. That reframes the whole matchup from 'wait until her escape is spent' to 'land the knockup and the escape does not matter'. I have stated this via the knockup rather than via the grounding flag on zac.json E, because grounding and knockup are different mechanics and only the knockup is supported by Riot's own description of the ability.
audit.corrected: Put the knockup-denies-the-blink rule into dosFull[2].d, whose title is 'E-knock her combo'.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.wants.foe[0] says Aurora wants to 'reset her passive on you'. Spirit Abjuration does not do anything to the target.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Aurora's spells and attacks exorcise spirits from the enemies she damages. Exorcised spirits follow Aurora around and heal her.' It is a heal on her, not a mark or a reset on Zac. The line as written invents a mechanic, and it also buries the fact _missing-interactions flags for this pairing — that Spirit Abjuration is the sustain Grievous Wounds has to answer.
audit.corrected: Rewrote wants.foe[0] and whys[3] around Spirit Abjuration as her heal, and added Grievous Wounds to report[8].t, which currently lists no anti-heal at all.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early says to 'build W stacks on the wave' and content.wants.you[1] says to 'Stack W on minion blobs'. Zac's W has no stacks.
audit.why: Unstable Matter is a flat 5 second cooldown at every rank with no charges and no stacking. The intended action is collecting the chunks Cell Division sheds. Identical error to the one in zac__akshan, which suggests a shared template rather than a one-off.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both around eating shed blobs.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.win gives Aurora all seven stages against a 52.71% Zac win rate — the only 7/0 chart in this slice — while full.phases[].side reads [Skill, Zac, Zac, Skill, Skill, Zac, Zac].
audit.why: A chart with no Zac row anywhere cannot coexist with Zac winning the matchup by nearly three points. Aurora does own the lane: Twofold Hex is 900 range against Zac's 800, Across the Veil dodges the engage, and Spirit Abjuration refunds the chip. But the item stages are where a tank with a revive passive starts converting, and the full layer already says so.
audit.corrected: content.win should read [Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Skill, Zac]. Not proposed as edits — categorical tokens cannot survive the length band.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.breakdown.cooldowns names the fabricated ability, gives it no number, and fills the other two bullets with 'Your committal tool' and 'Your ultimate' placeholders.
audit.why: Across the Veil at 22/21/20/19/18s is the longest non-ultimate cooldown in her kit and the actual window Zac plays for. The Weirding at 15s is the shorter second escape that ruins naive commits. Zac's own Elastic Slingshot is 21s at rank 1 — almost exactly as long as her blink, which is why trading E for W one-for-one is not the win the guide implies.
audit.corrected: Rebuilt the bullets around those three cooldowns.

audit.why: Same pasted-description bug as every other matchup in this slice, including the one card that carries the matchup's headline instruction.
audit.corrected: Rewrote all four to answer their own titles.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.trading and report[3].t all claim stomped blobs cost 'your passive revive margin'.
audit.why: Cell Division's shed chunks are sustain and destructible; the four bloblets appear only on fatal damage and set the revive. Stomping chunks costs sustain only. The 5 minute cooldown that governs the revive is what makes Zac able to survive a burst mage at all and it is written nowhere.

notes: SECOND fabricated ability name in this slice, same shape as zac__ambessa. 'Twofold Hunt' occupies 25 writable strings in champ-data/zac.full.js and is a corruption of Twofold Hex (Aurora's Q) attached to the W slot. The tell that makes the repair unambiguous is full.focus.letters = ['W'], which is correct — only the name was wrong, so Across the Veil is the right substitution and focus.letters needs no change. One edit could NOT be proposed: focus.text is 'Aurora Twofold Hunt' at 19 characters and the correct 'Aurora Across the Veil' is 22, which is +15.8% and outside the band. That string is what the loading screen displays, so it is the highest-visibility instance and it needs a manual write or a band exemption for focus.text specifically. Taken with zac__ambessa, two of the six matchups I audited carry a wholly invented enemy ability name repeated ~25 times each, and in both cases suspectNames was empty. The near-miss detector is scoring 'Twofold Hunt' against Aurora's real 'Twofold Hex' at edit distance 2 and still not flagging it, which suggests the check may only run against a subset of slots. Worth auditing the detector itself before trusting any 'suspectNames: []' in this dataset. Deliberately not asserted: whether Zac's Unstable Matter or Elastic Slingshot can damage Aurora while she is invisible after Across the Veil. Riot's text says invisible, not untargetable, which implies area damage still lands, but invisibility rules differ from Akali's untargetable shroud and aurora.json needsResearch is empty — this needs a wiki pass, not an inference. Nothing in champ-data was modified.
